name: The Oak of Na Cibulkach Forest Park

location.address: Lesopark Na Cibulkach (Prirodni park Kosire-Motol), south side of the path extending U Cibulky street near a crossroads, 150 00 Praha 5-Kosire

access: Free, public forest park (Prirodni park Kosire-Motol, designated 1991), open at all times
transport: Bus to Kosire, then a short walk into the Cibulka estate parkland
verify_notes: AOPK register kod 104880, protected since 21 June 2007, last register update 2024-08-22 (still listed alive/publishable). Planted around 1820 in the landscape park laid out at the Cibulka estate (usedlost Cibulka); the whole park became Prirodni park Kosire-Motol in 1991. Girth measured 394 cm in 2011 (per Czech Wikipedia, citing the AOPK register and the printed 'Pamatne stromy Prahy' 2011) and 408 cm in the register's 2024 update, consistent growth over 13 years. Height 24 m. Health noted as deteriorated in the 2011 source: shaded by neighbouring trees so the trunk is less massive than its neighbour, with an up-to-8-metre vertical crack down one side and a hollow at that point; still alive and standing per the 2024 register refresh, not a death signal. Long straight trunk that forks into three branches high up, carrying an elongated crown. Stands about 90 metres from its registered neighbour 'Dub s bizarnim kmenem Na Cibulkach' (delivered separately, prg_023), and a further group of three memorial oaks stands nearby in the same forest park (register kod 104881, recorded as a group of three so not delivered as an individual point). The two form a compact two-tree pocket in a public forest park that also holds the ruins of the Cibulka estate.

name: The Oak with the Bizarre Trunk of Na Cibulkach

location.address: Lesopark Na Cibulkach (Prirodni park Kosire-Motol), at a Y-shaped fork of the path extending U Cibulky street, west of the housing estate across an unnamed stream, 150 00 Praha 5-Kosire

access: Free, public forest park (Prirodni park Kosire-Motol, designated 1991), open at all times
transport: Bus to Kosire, then a short walk into the Cibulka estate parkland; 90 metres from prg_022
verify_notes: AOPK register kod 105315, protected since 19 March 2008, last register update 2024-08-22 (still listed alive/publishable), girth 525 cm agreeing exactly with the 2016 measurement recorded by prazskestromy.cz (Ing. Ales Rudl, entry 94) and cited on Czech Wikipedia. Planted around 1815 in the same Cibulka estate landscape park as prg_022, 90 metres away. Height 17 m. Name comes from its barrel-shaped trunk, which tapers and branches into a comparatively small crown; health also noted as deteriorated (2016 source), consistent with a veteran tree rather than a death signal, and the register's 2024 refresh still lists it as standing. Sits at a Y-shaped junction of forest paths, west of the housing estate across an unnamed stream.

name: The Beech of Brevnovska Gate, Hvezda

location.address: Obora Hvezda nature reserve, about 50 metres from the Brevnovska brana entrance (also called Vypisska or Prazska brana), on the main path toward the Hvezda summer palace, 162 00 Praha 6-Liboc

access: Free, public nature reserve (Obora Hvezda), open year round
transport: 10 min walk from the Obora Hvezda or Vypich tram and bus stops (same access as prg_005, about 230 metres away)
verify_notes: AOPK register kod 104291 (isop_id 52750), protected since 22 August 2001, last register update 2024-08-22 (still listed alive/publishable). One of the oldest beeches planted when the game reserve was restored and replanted with beech, oak and hornbeam sometime after 1763, following the destruction of the original stock first by French troops in the War of the Austrian Succession and then by Prussian troops in the Seven Years' War. Estimated age 210 to 250 years as of a 2016 assessment, revised to about 230 years in 2019; the same range this project already uses for prg_005 (The Twin Beech of Hvezda), a different, separately registered tree about 230 metres away near the same gate. Girth 373 cm (2009), 380 cm (2013), 386 cm per the register's 2024 update. Height 34 m in 2009, crown width 26 m, one of the tallest trees in the reserve. Health assessed very good in 2009 with no major visible damage; maintenance note recommends a safety/health pruning because it stands right beside the main path. Prominent buttressed root flare typical of old beeches. Stands about 50 metres inside the reserve from the Brevnovska gate, on the main path to the star-shaped Hvezda summer palace.

name: The Oak of Libocka Gate, Hvezda

location.address: Obora Hvezda nature reserve, right of the main path from the Libocka brana entrance toward the Hvezda summer palace, past the group of horse chestnuts and just before the large children's playground built in 2019, 162 00 Praha 6-Liboc

access: Free, public nature reserve (Obora Hvezda), open year round; Libocka gate reached from the Sidliste Petriny tram stop (lines 1 and 2) or on foot from Petriny metro station (line A)
transport: Sidliste Petriny tram stop, short walk into the reserve via the Libocka gate
verify_notes: AOPK register kod 104283 (isop_id 52728), protected since 2 October 2002, last register update 2024-08-22 (still listed alive/publishable). Officially registered and still recorded in the AOPK database as a Pedunculate Oak (dub letni, Quercus robur), but Czech Wikipedia notes the register's own 2015 update filed it under 'Data on individuals' as Quercus petraea (dub zimni, sessile oak), and that the register's own attached leaf photographs are clearly petiolate/stalked, the diagnostic feature of the sessile oak; flagging the species discrepancy rather than silently picking one. If the sessile-oak reading holds, Czech Wikipedia notes it would be the only sessile oak among the reserve's otherwise pedunculate-oak-dominated stands (oak makes up 57 percent of the reserve's trees by species, yet this is the reserve's only individually registered oak). Estimated age about 165 years as of 2016, roughly 175 by 2026. Girth 345 cm (2001), 352 cm (2009), 356 cm (2013, matching the register's current figure). Height 18 m, crown 16 m wide. Health: excellent apart from a few dry branches, actively maintained. Crooked, gnarled branches. Stands to the right of the main path from the Libocka gate toward the star-shaped Hvezda summer palace, just past a group of registered horse chestnuts and in front of a large children's playground built in 2019.
